title: Proof Before Permission: Quarantine Cannot Excuse Dog-Trade Gaps
excerpt: No verified incident record accompanies current trade defenses. Rabies control and pet protection demand traceable transport, quarantine, and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
Every stolen companion animal leaves a family searching, while every uninspected transport can weaken community biosecurity. Yet no police record, court judgment, seizure report, or official incident details accompany claims presented here about cyanide bait, pet-theft syndicates, or dog-farm supply. Those claims cannot be repeated as fact. They require records.

Myths Need Records, Not Repetition

“Farm-raised” does not prove lawful origin. A defensible supply chain needs traceable ownership, veterinary documentation, transport records, quarantine compliance, and inspection. Without those controls, animals may move through illegal channels, including theft and evasion. That is a regulatory failure, not proof that every dog in trade was stolen.

Biosecurity Has No Shortcut

Rabies exposure generally occurs when infected saliva enters a bite, scratch, broken skin, or mucous membrane. Handling sick animals, bite attacks, and uninspected slaughter create risks. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical care. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. See WHO guidance.

Vietnamese Families Deserve Enforceable Protection

Household rabies exposure and commercial-trade failures are separate dimensions of biosecurity vulnerability. Both demand accountable enforcement, transparent records, and protection for families and animals. SDE calls for complete national abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action and follow campaign updates reaching decision-makers.
